# Implementation Plan: PreToolUse — prioritize review-mail over arm when unreviewed mail is pending

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-10. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-pretooluse-prioritize-review-mail-over-arm/plan.md`.*

## Overview

The crews PreToolUse arm-first gate (`hooks/pre-tool-use.js::handleInput`) tells a lead/member to
ARM a background listener whenever `listenerState !== 'armed'`. But because listeners exit-on-delivery
(v1.2.9), the common path right after mail arrives is: the active listener delivers + exits → the next
tool call hits the arm-first gate → the generic "BLOCKED: arm a listener" block → the actor arms → the
arm re-delivers the still-pending mail + exits → next tool gated → arm again. A multi-turn, multi-token
loop. The productive action when unreviewed mail is pending is REVIEW-MAIL (already gate-exempt; drains
+ advances `lastReviewedSeq`), after which an arm stays blocking against a clean mailbox.

This change reorders WHICH guidance the arm-first gate surfaces: when the actor is unarmed AND has
unreviewed pending mail (`lastReviewRequiredSeq > lastReviewedSeq`), the block's PRIMARY instruction
becomes the engine-aware REVIEW-MAIL command (the byte-identical command the review-required nag emits),
with a SECONDARY "then arm against a clean mailbox" note. When no mail is pending, the existing plain
arm block is emitted unchanged. It is a block-MESSAGE + gate-ORDER change, not a new capability — the
arm-first safety stays intact (the actor is still told to arm, just after draining).

### Technical Constraints
- PreToolUse dropped its own review-required ENFORCEMENT in v1.5.6 (Stop owns it). This change does NOT
  re-introduce PreToolUse review-required enforcement — it only changes the message shown when the
  arm-first gate already fires (unarmed). It must NOT consult `CREWS_REVIEW_MODE` (that gates Stop
  enforcement; the arm-first gate fires regardless of review mode).
- The new branch must sit AFTER the `isReviewMailCall` bypass (`:451`), the listener-output-inspection
  bypass (`:457-463`), the AskUserQuestion intercept (`:471-474`), and the `listenerState === 'armed'`
  early-return (`:475`), so an actor actually running review-mail still passes, the AskUserQuestion
  routing is unchanged, and the branch only fires when unarmed.
- The v3.4 lead-unconditional-listener gate is in `hooks/stop.js` — untouched.
- crews has no tsconfig; "typecheck" = `node --check <changed .js>`.

## Approach

### Architecture
Insert a single new branch in `hooks/pre-tool-use.js::handleInput` immediately after the
`if (listenerState === 'armed') return;` line and before the plain arm block. Read the `manifest`
ONCE (move/keep the existing `const manifest = readManifest(...)` above the new branch) and reuse it
for both the new branch and the plain arm block — no extra read. In the new branch, call
`reviewRequiredReason(state.name, crew, cwd, state.role, manifest)`; if it returns non-null (unreviewed
mail pending), build a combined block whose body is `[reviewReason, '', <arm note>]` and emit it via
`block(...)` + an `appendLog` line, then `return`. If it returns null (no mail pending), fall through
to the existing plain arm block unchanged.

The arm note (secondary) reuses the already-built `buildListenerCommand({...})` `cmd` so the actor sees
the exact arm command to run AFTER draining, preserving arm-first safety. To keep the arm command and
the engine-aware shell prose available to both the new branch and the plain arm block, build `cmd` +
`armBlock` before the new branch (they are pure string construction with no side effects) and reference
them from both paths. The combined review-mail-first reason is, in order:
1. the full `reviewRequiredReason(...)` string (headline + engine-aware review-mail command + cursor
   prose) — byte-identical to the review-required nag,
2. a blank line,
3. a short "Once your mailbox is drained, arm a fresh listener so you stay reachable:" line followed by
   the `armBlock` lines (the same engine-aware arm instruction),
4. a closing line noting the freshly-armed listener then stays blocking against the now-clean mailbox.

### Implementation Strategy
1. Add `reviewRequiredReason` to the destructured import from `./protocol/review-gate` at the top of
   `hooks/pre-tool-use.js` (currently `parseReviewMode`/etc. are imported in stop.js; pre-tool-use does
   not yet import review-gate — add `const { reviewRequiredReason } = require('./protocol/review-gate');`).
2. In `handleInput`, hoist the `const manifest = readManifest(...)` and the `cmd`/`armBlock`
   construction to just after the `listenerState === 'armed'` early-return, before the new branch.
3. Insert the review-mail-first branch (call `reviewRequiredReason`, build combined reason, `appendLog`,
   `block`, `return`) before the plain arm block.
4. Leave the plain arm block as the fall-through (reused `cmd`/`armBlock`).
5. Add a new test file and audit existing tests.

## Risk Areas
- **Test flip (CONFIRMED, High):** `review-gate.test.js` lines ~367-381
  (`crews-review-gate-pretool-before-listener`) seeds review-required mail + `listenerState: 'exited'`
  (unarmed) and asserts `must arm a background listener` (:379) plus NO `review-required` (:380) — the
  new branch flips both, so `node tests/run.js` fails unless this test is updated. Mitigation: US-002
  explicitly updates this block AND broadens the audit to a tests/-tree grep for
  `you must arm a background listener` / `lastReviewRequiredSeq` / `lastReviewedSeq`. The four armed
  mode-tests just above it stay green (armed early-return short-circuits).
- **Double manifest read:** avoid by hoisting the single `readManifest` above the new branch.
- **Command divergence vs Stop:** avoided by reusing `reviewRequiredReason` (single source of truth) —
  do NOT hand-build the review-mail command in pre-tool-use.
- **Ordering regression:** the new branch must go after the review-mail bypass, listener-output bypass,
  AskUserQuestion intercept, and armed early-return; AC pins each is preserved.
- **Lead vs member:** the gate applies to both; the operator-flagged case is a LEAD. `reviewRequiredReason`
  is role-aware; AC covers a lead fixture.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: When `listenerState !== 'armed'` AND `lastReviewRequiredSeq > lastReviewedSeq`, the PreToolUse
  block reason BEGINS WITH (as a contiguous prefix) the exact string returned by
  `reviewRequiredReason(state.name, crew, cwd, state.role, manifest)` (the engine-aware review-mail
  command + headline + cursor prose), and does NOT lead with the plain
  `BLOCKED: you must arm a background listener` text. Verified by a test that seeds an unarmed member
  with `lastReviewRequiredSeq=2, lastReviewedSeq=1` and asserts the block reason starts with the direct
  `reviewRequiredReason(...)` output.
- AC2: When `listenerState !== 'armed'` AND NO mail is pending (`lastReviewRequiredSeq <= lastReviewedSeq`,
  e.g. both 0/unset), the PreToolUse block reason is the existing plain arm block (contains
  `you must arm a background listener`) and does NOT contain the review-mail command. Verified by a test.
- AC3: When `listenerState === 'armed'`, no block is emitted regardless of review seqs (the armed
  early-return short-circuits before the new branch). Verified by a regression test.
- AC4: The review-mail-first block's leading segment is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the value returned by a DIRECT
  call to `reviewRequiredReason(name, crew, cwd, role, manifest)` for the same manifest/env — i.e. the
  block equals `<reviewRequiredReason output>` + the secondary arm note (NOT a hand-rebuilt command).
  The test asserts this across the explicit matrix: engine ∈ {claude, copilot, codex} × CREWS_BIN
  env-set (useEnvBin=true) and env-unset (useEnvBin=false), so the per-engine token is exercised
  (`$CREWS_BIN` for claude, `$env:CREWS_BIN` for copilot/codex, absolute dispatcher path when
  env-unset). The comparison MUST be against direct `reviewRequiredReason(...)` output — do NOT reuse
  or extend `review-gate.test.js`'s `expectedReviewRequiredReason` helper (it special-cases only
  `engine === 'copilot'` and would produce the wrong codex arm-prefix).
- AC5: The new block still instructs the actor to arm AFTER draining (arm-first safety preserved): the
  block contains the arm command/instruction (the same engine-aware `armBlock`) as a secondary note.
- AC6: The existing review-mail bypass (`isReviewMailCall`), listener-output-inspection bypass, and
  AskUserQuestion intercept are unchanged (no regression). Verified by the existing suites staying green.
- AC7: A LEAD fixture (unarmed + review pending) also receives the review-mail-first block (not just
  members). Verified by a test.
- AC8: The flipped existing test `review-gate.test.js` `crews-review-gate-pretool-before-listener`
  (lines ~367-381) is updated to expect the review-mail-first block, and the broadened tests/-tree
  audit grep (AC's three tokens) finds no other un-updated flip. `node tests/run.js` passes (full
  suite green); `node --check` passes on the changed `.js` files.
- AC9: The crews version is bumped to 3.20.0 and `tests/version.test.js` passes. `scripts/bump-version.js`
  edits 7 files total (3 plugin manifests: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.github/plugin/plugin.json`,
  `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`; 3 marketplace indexes: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`,
  `.github/plugin/marketplace.json`, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`; plus `tests/version.test.js`),
  and `CHANGELOG.md` + `AGENTS.md` (the v3.20.0 section + a common-mistake gotcha) are updated consistently.
